plain_text:
COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES 
 
NOVEMBER 12TH, 2026 
ROOM 208, CITY HALL 
229 MAIN STREET, NASHUA, NH 03060 
 
Members Present: Matt Sullivan, Liz Hannum, Kristy Besada, Shoshanna Kelly, Kyle Schneck 
Staff Present: Jessica Connors 
Public Present: Joe Tamposi 
 
Call to Order 
M. Sullivan called the meeting to order at 5:07PM as quorum was present. 
 
Discussion: Land Bank Update 
• L. Hannum provided a brief update on the land bank survey.  
• The City is evaluating different land bank models to determine which may be most 
appropriate for Nashua. Several potential project examples are being analyzed for 
viability. 
• Discussions about the legality of the city owning a land bank are in preliminary stages; 
the project contractor will also be determining the legality of tax -deeded properties 
entering the land bank. 
• Phase 1 of the process will likely take two to three months and is expected to wrap up in 
January. 
• The committee discussed whether an application should be submitted for Phase 2, or if 
the committee itself should pursue the project. 
• The committee determined that it would be helpful to have the contractors present the 
results of Phase 1.  
Discussion: Adaptive Reuse and Road to Rehousing Act 
• The committee briefly discussed adaptive reuse projects in Nashua and throughout New 
England. 
• L. Hannum requested an update about the Road to Housing Act update; M. Sullivan will 
present an update at the next meeting. 
Discussion: Commitment Letter & Closing Process
• M. Sullivan discussed potential updates to the commitment letter and loan closing 
process. 
• M. Sullivan noted that the committee’s fee structure needs to be clearer. Updated fees 
have not yet been determined, but J. Connors and M. Sullivan are researching fee 
structures used by similar committees and are working with the City's legal team to revise 
the commitment letter. 
• M. Sullivan suggested the committee revisit previous discussions on rates before making 
another loan. 
• S. Kelly suggested that M. Sullivan make a presentation at a Board of Aldermen meeting 
so that the aldermen can see some of the work being done by the committee; M. Sullivan 
agreed and stated that the Human Affairs Committee might have space for a presentation 
in the near future. S. Kelly will discuss the idea with Alderman Lopez.  
Discussion: Avery on the River 
• Joe Tamposi of Tamposi Brothers Holdings presented Avery on the River, a 50-unit 
affordable housing project seeking $1.6 million dollars from the committee.  
• The project is located at 60 Crown Street and will be located directly across from their 
previous project, Avery Lane.  
• M. Sullivan clarified that while no decision will be made tonight, the committee hopes to 
make a final decision by the December or January meeting. 
• J. Tamposi noted that the $1.6 million request is the final piece of the project’s financing. 
Other sources include 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, New Hampshire Housing’s 
Opioid Use Disorder Supportive Housing Capital Program, and a developer loan. 
• J. Tamposi described the project as income-averaged, with all units designated as 
affordable and an average affordability level of 60% AMI. He also discussed the market 
study and noted that Avery Lane leased up quickly due to the demand for affordable 
housing in Nashua. 
• J. Tamposi discussed the development budget. He stated that the project is efficient and 
that they were confident in the construction numbers, as they’ve recently done several 
other similar projects, including Avery Lane. 
• Construction for the project is estimated to start in May 2027 if all the financing can be 
secured.  
• M. Sullivan and K. Schneck discussed the levy near the project.  
• J. Tamposi’s ultimate request is for $1.6 million at a 4% interest rate over a 20-year term, 
repaid with surplus cash flow. He noted that they are flexible regarding when the funds 
would be made available to the project. 
• Committee members asked several questions at the end of the presentation, including 
questions about where the developers would look for additional funding if they didn’t get 
a loan from the committee, the construction firm, environmental cleanup, and the 
developer’s understanding of the Opioid Use Disorder Supportive Housing Capital 
Program. 
• J. Tamposi noted that they have also applied for $1.6 million in capital subsidy from New 
Hampshire Housing. If awarded funding from a source that does not trigger Build 
America, Buy America (BABA) requirements, they may withdraw their application to the 
HRF Committee.  
• J. Tamposi noted that BABA would add approximately $300,000 to the budget.
• M. Sullivan requested that J. Tamposi keep the committee updated about their capital 
subsidy request.  
 
Non-Public Session: Marguerite’s Place 
• S. Kelly made a motion to go into a non-public session to discuss matters which if 
discussed in public could potentially or would likely affect adversely the reputation of 
any person other than a member of this public body pursuant with RSA 91A(3)(2)(C). 
i. L. Hannum offered a Second to the motion. 
ii. A roll call was taken, which resulted as follows: 
1. Yea: 5  
2. Nay: 0 
Motion Carried 
 
Non-Public Session Sealing of Minutes  
• M. Sullivan accepted a Motion to seal the minutes of the non-public session from S. 
Kelly. L. Hannum offered a second to the motion. 
o A roll call was taken, which resulted as follows: 
▪ Yea: 5 
▪ Nay: 0 
Motion Carried 
 
Vote: Marguerite’s Place 
• K. Schneck made a motion to offer a $500,000 loan to Marguerite’s Place, with loan 
terms to be determined after further discussion with Marguerite’s Place. 
i. K. Besada offered a Second to the motion. 
ii. A roll call was taken, which resulted as follows: 
1. Yea: 4 
2. Nay: 1 
Motion Carried 
 
Discussion: Next Meeting Date 
• The committee discussed which dates work best for them going forward; K. Schneck 
suggested an early morning meeting might work better. 
• M. Sullivan suggested floating a 7:30AM meeting by the remainder of the committee 
members.  
• The next meeting date was determined to be either December 4th at 7:30AM or 
December 7th at 5PM, subject to the availability of the remaining committee members. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:15 PM.  
 
Next meeting: The next meeting date is under discussion.
